sentences.text:
Author: T. Vinod Kumar
Bench: T. Vinod Kumar
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice T. Vinod Kumar
 Writ Petition No.25753 Of 2024
Order:

Heard learned Counsel for the petitioners, learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing on behalf of respondent Nos.1 to 6, learned Government Pleader for Mines & Geology appearing on behalf of respondent No.7, Sri P. Sri Harsha Reddy, learned Standing Counsel appearing on behalf of respondent Nos.8 and 9 and perused the record.
2. Shorn of unnecessary details, the case of the petitioners in brief, is that at an earlier point of time the respondents had issued notifications for acquiring the land admeasuring Ac.708.16 Gts. under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 and an Award has been passed on 16.09.2015 which included the lands of the petitioners.

3. Petitioners further contend that on a challenge being made to the aforesaid Award, this Court by its order dated 15.11.2022, recording the submission of the learned Standing Counsel appearing on behalf of the respondent No.6 that the aforesaid land is not required and since no possession of the said land has been taken, had allowed the Writ Petition by setting aside the Award and also held that the petitioners are entitled to exercise their right of ownership over their respective extents of land including seeking of mutation, updation of Dharani portal and issue of pattadar passbooks and title deeds etc.,
4.

Petitioners further contend that after the disposal of the aforesaid Writ Petition, the respondent authorities have now initiated acquisition proceedings afresh for acquiring the land admeasuring Ac.88.20 Gts. by issuing preliminary notification dated 14.03.2024 and thereafter have issued draft declaration dated 29.06.2024.

5. Petitioners further contend that even though the land of the petitioners was acquired under an Award earlier, since, the said Award was set aside by this Court, the name of the 8th respondent cannot be shown as owner of subject land without correcting the same in the fresh proceedings initiated; and thus, the petitioners apprehend that the authorities would proceed further on the basis of the aforesaid notification issued with incorrect details/information; that the petitioners had submitted a representation to the respondent authorities on 11.09.2024 by sending the same through Registered Post bringing to the notice of the authorities the aforesaid facts and sought for making necessary corrections while proceeding further on the basis of the aforesaid preliminary notification and approved declaration.

sentences.text:
It is the further contention of the petitioners that though the authorities have issued preliminary notification under Section 11 and draft declaration under Section 19 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short 'the Act'), no notice has been issued to them as required under Section 21 of the Act , to enable them to submit their objections and as such the entire proceedings are vitiated and are liable to be stayed.
7. Per contra, learned Standing Counsel and the learned Government Pleader appearing on behalf of respondents submits that though at an earlier point of time the authorities had acquired large extent of land admeasuring 708.16 Gts. which includes the land of the petitioners by passing an Award dated 26.09.2015

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
, since the said extent of land was no more required, the said Award was not acted upon by taking possession and paying compensation thereunder and as such, the authorities have now issued fresh notification proposing to acquire a smaller extent of land admeasuring Ac.88.20 Gts only.
8. On behalf of the respondents, it is contended that the authorities while issuing preliminary notification and draft declaration have caused notification on 29.06.2024 in terms of the provisions of Section 3(v) of the Act and thus, if the petitioners had any objections to the draft declaration issued under Section 19 of the Act they ought to have filed their objections thereto within the time prescribed thereunder.
9. On behalf of the respondents, it is further contended that in terms of the provisions of Section 21 of Act, no individual notices are required unless and until the person interested is residing elsewhere whereupon only the Collector is required to send the notice to him by post at his last known address and inasmuch as the petitioners do not claim falling under the aforesaid category of person specified under Section 21(v) of the Act, the claim of the petitioners of, they not being issued any individual notices cannot be accepted as the authorities have caused public notice inviting claims to compensation and R&R scheme in respect of all persons interested.

10. Learned Government Pleader also submits that the petitioners by their own admission on learning of one of the interested person having been issued with a notice under Section 21 of the Act claim to have submitted representation dated 11.09.2024, the authorities would consider the said representation and take further action while passing the Award in terms of Section 23 and 30 of the Act.
11. I have taken note of the respective contentions urged.
12. Before adverting to the respective contentions, it is necessary to note that the scope of Section 21 of the Act dealing with notice to persons interested.

The provision prescribes that the Collector shall publish the public notice on his website or cause such public notice to be given at convenient places on or near the land to be taken and does not mandate giving of any personal notices to the persons whose lands are sought to be acquired, more so as preliminary notification issued Section 11 and draft declaration under Section 19 are required to be published by way of a notification; and that the term 'notification' having been defined under Section 3(v) of the Act as being in official gazette.

sentences.text: 2 Thus, the claim of the petitioners of the authorities requiring to issue personal notices to the persons interested, whose lands are sought to be acquired does not appear to this Court to be the scheme of the Act, for this Court to approve the contention advanced on behalf of the petitioners.

Accordingly,
the said contention is rejected.

13. However, taking note of the fact that Section 21(2) of the Act provides that upon public notice being issued, which in normal circumstances as indicated in sub-section 1 of Section 21 is by putting the same on the website of the Collector or by displaying it at a convenient place on or near the place of acquisition which normally includes the same being displayed in the Gram panchayat office, the Thasil office, R.D.O. office which are considered as public places, the same would be construed as sufficient compliance of Section 21 of Act.

Since, the petitioners themselves admit of learning of the notice issued under Section 21 of the Act from one of the persons interested and having approached the respondent authorities by submitting representation dated 11.09.2024, it is not open for the petitioners to claim that since such notice was not issued to him, the entire proceeding to be vitiated requiring it to be stayed by this Court,
14.

However, taking note of the fact that sub-section 2 of Section 21 of the Act mandates such notice to be issued with minimum of 30 days time and maximum of six months, and the petitioners having submitted their representation dated 11.09.2024, this Court is of the view that the representation submitted by the petitioner on 11.09.2024 being within the time mentioned under the Act, is required to be considered including as to the change of name of SCCL, Ramagundam Open Cast II Project land, recorded as pattadar in the revenue records based on the Award passed earlier is required to be altered, reflecting the names of the original pattadars prior to the acquisition undertaken earlier under the Award dated 26.09.2014, before taking further action in the matter.

15. Further, it is also to be noted that since the petitioners are now aware of the contents of the public notice and inasmuch as six months time has not been elapsed, the petitioners are at liberty to approach the respondent authorities and submit relevant information/ documents as sought for under the aforesaid notice issued under Section 21 of the Act for consideration of the authorities.
16. Subject to the above direction, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
No costs.

Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this Writ Petition shall stand closed.
__________________ T. VINOD KUMAR, J Date: 07.11.2024 MRKR Puli Rajesham vs The State Of Telangana on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185116963/
